terra.problem: Moses being their brother is not stated in this passage and needs a Scripture reference.
The line about family business getting loud relies on a family stereotype.
“Not even close” is a negative response to the baker’s answer.
The oven-timer joke does not make sense as a comparison: the timer going off is not someone overhearing a conversation.
The text says the LORD spoke suddenly, but does not say there was no warning at all.
The passage does not mention a river; it does not establish that there is no river in the scene.
Calling Moses their brother states a fact not given in this passage without a reference.
“No guessing at what it means” goes beyond the LORD saying He speaks clearly and not in riddles.
Calling Moses Aaron’s brother states a fact not given in this passage without a reference.
“That takes some nerve” puts Aaron down for his plea.
Joshua is not mentioned in the scene, but the text does not establish that he is absent.
“Nobody else is part of that moment” goes beyond the text; Miriam is also present, and the passage does not establish who else may be there.
Calling Miriam Moses’ sister states a fact not given in this passage without a reference.
The claim that forty appears often in the Bible is a fact outside the passage and needs a reference.
The people not moving on does not mean nobody takes a step.
